Lessons.Title: More Movement
ExplanationParagraphs: Source-aligned goals: Create an equation to represent the vertical and horizontal translations needed to move one graph to another. Describe the effect on a graph by replacing $f(x)$ with $f(x)+k$ and $f(x+k)$.
A model g(x)=f(x-h)+k shifts f right h and up k. A negative value of h or k reverses the direction; coordinates of identifiable features change consistently.

Source activity 3.1: Moving a Graph: How can we translate the graph of \(A\) to match one of the other graphs? Explain the mathematical model, verify the relevant result and have a teacher inspect original diagrams or discussion evidence.

Source activity 3.2: New Hours for the Kitchen: Remember the bakery with the thermostat set to \(65^\circ \text{F}\)? At 5:00 a.m., the temperature in the kitchen rises to \(85^\circ \text{F}\) due to the ovens and other kitchen equipment being used until they are turned off at 10:00 a.m. When the owner decided to open 2 hours earlier, the baking schedule changed to match. Andre thinks, “When the bakery starts baking 2… Explain the mathematical model, verify the relevant result and have a teacher inspect original diagrams or discussion evidence.

Source activity 3.3: Thawing Meat: A piece of meat is taken out of the freezer to thaw. The data points show its temperature \(M\), in degrees Fahrenheit, \(t\) hours after it was taken out. The graph \(M=G(t)\), where \(G(t) = \text-62(0.85)^t\), models the shape of the data but is in the wrong position. Jada thinks changing the equation to \(J(t)=\text-62(0.85)^t + 75.1\) makes a good model for the data. Noah… Explain the mathematical model, verify the relevant result and have a teacher inspect original diagrams or discussion evidence.
